routines.title: Introductory Post-Easy-Run Downshift Reset
routines.summary: Cooldown Routine session focusing on gradual recovery, relaxation.
routines.riskReason: Controlled movement patterns maintain safe tissue loading.

sessionStructure.name: Deep Diaphragmatic Breathing
notes: Avoid rushing the return phase of the exercise.

sessionStructure.name: Standing Quad Stretch
notes: Focus on perfect posture and form quality.

easierVariant.description: Reduce total exercise sets from 3 to 2 to manage local muscular fatigue.
modifications: Increase rest intervals between sets if needed.

harderVariant.description: Increase total sets from 3 to 4 or add minor load resistance.
modifications: Increase work volume by running 4 sets.
Maintain slower eccentric controls under loaded sets.

coachingNotes: A proper cooldown supports the gradual transition of the body from running to rest.
Downshift breathing depth dynamically to facilitate active restoration.
Gentle walking is highly effective to slowly drop heart rate curves.
commonMistakes: Rushing through the repetitions, which ruins correct movement form.
Holding your breath, which creates excessive thoracic pressure.
Neglecting proper joint alignment, placing shear load on knees or back.
safetyNotes: Listen to physical feedback; never push past sharp joint pain.
Ensure equipment is clean and weights are safely controlled.
Stop execution immediately if feeling dizzy or lightheaded.
